newsitem.title: POLAND: Furniture maker Fameg to offer shares in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Furniture maker Fameg to offer shares in Q1 1997.

text.p: Polish medium-size furniture maker Fameg SA plans a public share offering in the first quarter of next year, the company said on Friday.

"An issue prospectus should be submitted to the Securities Commission this year and a subscription is planned for the first quarter of 1997," it said in a statement. Fameg seeks listing on the bourse's parallel market.
Fameg, based in the central town of Radomsko, is controlled by one of 15 investment funds created under Poland's mass privatisation programme.

The statement said HSBC Investment Services would be Fameg's financial adviser, while Reiffeisen Zentralbank Osterreich AG and Polish Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) would jointly manage the issue. KPMG firm will be Fameg's auditor.
The furniture maker, exporting 80 percent of its output, netted 3.7 million zlotys in 1995 on sales of 87.1 million zlotys, the statement said. No comparative figures were given.
The fund controlling Fameg, Progress SA, plans to list a total of 12 firms on the Warsaw bourse out of more than 30 firms it runs and another 12 on the over-the-counter market.
